subject.title: fix(config): bound external catalog file reads with size limit

question: Should an over-limit external catalog be silently ignored, or should the bounded-read hardening retain the limit while emitting a visible diagnostic for the resulting changed auto-enable selection?
rationale: The size limit is a security control, but the current caller deliberately swallows read failures; deciding whether a valid existing catalog may disappear silently is an upgrade and operator-contract choice.

options.title: Reject with a visible diagnostic
options.body: Keep the 16 MiB bound and surface a concise operator-visible warning when a configured catalog is skipped, with regression coverage for the resulting selection behavior.

options.title: Accept silent compatibility change
options.body: Keep the current catch-and-continue behavior and explicitly accept that oversized configured catalogs no longer influence auto-enable precedence.

options.title: Pause for config-owner direction
options.body: Hold this PR until the config-selection owner chooses the desired diagnostic and upgrade contract.

recommendation.title: Reject with a visible diagnostic
recommendation.body: Keep the 16 MiB bound and surface a concise operator-visible warning when a configured catalog is skipped, with regression coverage for the resulting selection behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged bounded-read work is the closest available history signal for balancing file-bound hardening with preserved symlink and operator behavior.
